summary.en: Supports roots beside the tidal channel.
summary.zh: 承托潮沟旁的树根。

detail.en: The mudbank supports the roots, with a lower channel along its front. Rising tide covers more of its surface. [S27, S30]
detail.zh: 泥岸承托树根，前缘有较低的潮沟。潮水升高时，会盖住更多泥面。[S27, S30]

summary.en: Covers and exposes mud as the tide changes.
summary.zh: 随潮水涨退，覆盖或露出泥面。

detail.en: Tides change conditions around the mudbank. Switch between low and high water to compare the exposed mud. Both views keep the same food links. [S27, S30]
detail.zh: 潮水涨退会改变泥岸周围的条件。切换低水位和高水位，比较露出的泥面。两种画面保留相同的食物关系。[S27, S30]

summary.en: Provides a hiding place for fiddler crabs.
summary.zh: 为招潮蟹提供藏身处。

detail.en:
Fiddler crabs retreat into burrows at high tide. The crab can be hidden while its burrow opening remains visible. [S5]

Only the opening is shown here. [S30]
detail.zh:
高潮时，招潮蟹会退入洞中。蟹藏起来时，画面仍保留洞口。[S5]

这里只显示洞口。[S30]

summary.en: Makes food and releases salt through its leaves.
summary.zh: 制造食物，并通过叶片排盐。

detail.en:
Api-api Putih (Avicennia alba) has salt glands in its leaves. These help it excrete salt. Different mangrove kinds handle salt in different ways. [S3]

Shallow side roots join its upright, pencil-shaped breathing roots. [S2, S3]
detail.zh:
Api-api Putih（Avicennia alba）的叶片有盐腺，帮助它排出盐分。不同红树处理盐的方式不同。[S3]

浅层侧根与直立的铅笔状呼吸根相连。[S2, S3]

summary.en: Joins the tree to its breathing roots.
summary.zh: 连接树体与呼吸根。

detail.en:
Avicennia alba has shallow side roots beneath the mud. Upright breathing roots grow from them. [S3]

The cutaway shows how these roots join. [S30]
detail.zh:
Avicennia alba 的浅层侧根在泥下延伸，直立的呼吸根从侧根长出。[S3]

剖面显示这些根怎样连接。[S30]

summary.en: Takes in oxygen above the mud.
summary.zh: 在泥面上方吸收氧气。

detail.en:
Pencil-shaped breathing roots grow upright from shallow side roots. They reach above the mud and take in oxygen. [S2, S3]

Follow each root down to see its connection beneath the mud. [S30]
detail.zh:
铅笔状呼吸根从浅层侧根向上长出，伸出泥面吸收氧气。[S2, S3]

沿着每根呼吸根往下看，可以找到它在泥下的连接。[S30]

summary.en: Makes food and supplies leaves.
summary.zh: 制造食物并供应叶片。

detail.en:
Bakau Minyak has prop roots reaching down from its trunk. Mangrove trees provide shelter and leaves that can become food. [S2, S6, S8]

Its food-web node supplies new leaf material. Removing it leaves old fallen leaves in the scene. [S30]
detail.zh:
Bakau Minyak 的支柱根从树干向下伸出。红树提供庇护，叶片也能成为食物。[S2, S6, S8]

它的食物网节点供应新的叶片物质。移走节点后，画面仍保留旧落叶。[S30]

summary.en: Anchors the tree and shelters young animals.
summary.zh: 固定树体，并庇护幼小动物。

detail.en:
Bakau prop roots reach from the trunk towards the mud and anchor the tree. Spaces between the roots shelter young animals. [S2]

Compare them with the pencil-shaped roots of the neighbouring Api-api. [S30]
detail.zh:
Bakau 的支柱根从树干伸向泥地，固定树体。根之间的空隙能庇护幼小动物。[S2]

可以与旁边 Api-api 的铅笔状根比较。[S30]

summary.en: Provides food after leaves fall.
summary.zh: 叶片掉落后仍能提供食物。

detail.en:
Some mangrove crabs eat fallen leaves and break them into smaller pieces. Dead leaves still contain food energy. [S6, S24]

Old leaves remain when you remove the continuing leaf supply. The calculation leaves out their decay rate. [S30]
detail.zh:
有些红树林蟹吃落叶，把叶弄成较小的碎片。死叶仍含有食物中的能量。[S6, S24]

移走持续的叶片供应后，旧落叶仍会保留。计算没有包括它们的分解速率。[S30]

summary.en: Makes food using sunlight.
summary.zh: 利用阳光制造食物。

detail.en:
Algae use sunlight to make food. Some fiddler crabs and climbing crabs eat algae, as recorded in different observations. [S7, S18, S24]

The patch represents algae on the mud surface. [S30]
detail.zh:
藻类利用阳光制造食物。不同观察记录到，一些招潮蟹和攀爬蟹类会吃藻类。[S7, S18, S24]

这个斑块代表泥面上的藻类。[S30]

summary.en: Feeds with a small claw; the male displays a large claw.
summary.zh: 用小螯取食；雄蟹用大螯展示。

detail.en:
A male fiddler crab has one enlarged claw and a smaller feeding claw. It also has eye stalks and four pairs of walking legs. [S5, S32]

At high tide, it hides in its burrow. The single crab shape represents the group. [S5, S30]
detail.zh:
雄招潮蟹有一只大螯和一只取食小螯，还有眼柄和四对步足。[S5, S32]

高潮时，它藏进洞里。图中用一只蟹代表这一组生物。[S5, S30]

summary.en: Eats leaf material and climbs above rising water.
summary.zh: 吃叶片，也会爬到涨水水面上方。

detail.en:
This group brings together several climbing-crab kinds. Some eat leaves; others graze on algae. The leaf-feeding record comes from Sungei Buloh. These records do not give one Episesarma species a fixed diet of both foods. [S6, S7]

The crab has four pairs of walking legs and two claws. At high water, it moves up the Bakau trunk. [S32, S30]
detail.zh:
这一组包含几类攀爬蟹。有些吃叶片，有些刮食藻类。叶片取食的记录来自双溪布洛。这些记录不表示同一种 Episesarma 固定吃这两种食物。[S6, S7]

蟹有四对步足和一对螯。高水位时，它沿 Bakau 树干向上移。[S32, S30]

summary.en: Moves across mud with fleshy pectoral fins.
summary.zh: 用肉质胸鳍在泥面移动。

detail.en:
Giant mudskippers are fish. Their modified gill chambers and skin help them breathe out of water. Fleshy pectoral fins help them move over mud. [S4]

General guides list crabs as food. Local diet samples differ, so the crab-to-fish arrows show possible feeding relationships. [S4, S13, S31]
detail.zh:
弹涂鱼是鱼。特化的鳃腔和皮肤帮助它离水呼吸，肉质胸鳍帮助它在泥面移动。[S4]

一般指南把蟹列为食物，当地食物样本却有差异。因此，蟹到鱼的箭头表示可能的取食关系。[S4, S13, S31]

summary.en: Catches food with a long neck and bill.
summary.zh: 借助长颈和长喙捕食。

detail.en:
Herons have long necks and bills. They eat fish and crustaceans. NParks lists herons among the giant mudskipper’s predators. [S4, S29]

The two-legged bird represents herons as a group. [S30]
detail.zh:
鹭有长颈和长喙，吃鱼和甲壳类。NParks 把鹭列为弹涂鱼的捕食者。[S4, S29]

图中这只两腿的鸟代表鹭类。[S30]

summary.en: Provides another possible food for larger animals.
summary.zh: 为较大的动物提供另一种可能的食物。

detail.en:
Herons and giant mudskippers can eat small fish. Real animals may have more food choices than a short food web shows. [S4, S29]

This small fish lies outside the food-web calculation. [S30]
detail.zh:
鹭和弹涂鱼都可能吃小鱼。真实动物的食物选择可能比简短食物网上显示的更多。[S4, S29]

这条小鱼没有加入食物网计算。[S30]

summary.en: Breaks down leaf material and obtains energy.
summary.zh: 分解叶片物质并获得能量。

detail.en:
Bacteria help break down mangrove leaf litter. They obtain energy from the organic material as it decomposes. [S10]

This close-up uses enlarged shapes to make them visible. [S30]
detail.zh:
细菌参与红树林落叶的分解，从分解中的有机物获得能量。[S10]

近景把它们放大，方便观察。[S30]

summary.en: Breaks down dead organic material.
summary.zh: 分解死亡的有机物质。

detail.en:
Fungi help break down mangrove leaf litter. They obtain energy from organic material, without using photosynthesis to make food. [S10]

The branching threads are an enlarged diagram. [S30]
detail.zh:
真菌参与红树林落叶的分解。它们从有机物获得能量，不通过光合作用制造食物。[S10]

分枝的丝体是放大示意图。[S30]

summary.en: Retains water to help the fish breathe out of water.
summary.zh: 保留水分，帮助鱼离水呼吸。

detail.en:
The giant mudskipper’s modified gill chambers and gas exchange through its skin help it breathe out of water. It is a fish. [S4]

This enlarged diagram shows a cavity, without the detailed gill anatomy. [S30]
detail.zh:
弹涂鱼特化的鳃腔和皮肤气体交换，帮助它离水呼吸。它是鱼。[S4]

这个放大的空腔是示意，没有显示详细鳃部结构。[S30]

summary.en: Marks a place to observe the habitat.
summary.zh: 标示观察生境的位置。

detail.en: The boardwalk edge suggests observing without collecting animals. It is part of the display setting. [S30]
detail.zh: 步道边缘提示观察时把动物留在原处。它是展示场景的一部分。[S30]

summary.en: Supports the habitat and enlarged close-ups.
summary.zh: 承托生境和放大近景。

detail.en: This display stand supports the habitat and the separate enlarged diagrams. [S30]
detail.zh: 展示台承托生境和旁边独立的放大示意图。[S30]

note.en: Fallen leaves pass from the living tree to leaf-eating crabs.
note.zh: 活树的落叶供吃叶的蟹取食。

note.en: Some climbing-crab kinds graze on algae. This group includes several kinds, with different diets.
note.zh: 一些攀爬蟹类会刮食藻类。这一组包含不同蟹类，食物也不同。

note.en: Algae feeding has been observed in fiddler crabs outside Singapore.
note.zh: 新加坡以外曾观察到招潮蟹吃藻类。

note.en: General guides list crabs as food, though the Lim Chu Kang sample contained no fiddlers.
note.zh: 一般指南把蟹列为食物，但林厝港样本中没有检出招潮蟹。

note.en: A mudskipper was reported taking an Episesarma crab when the opportunity arose. The report gives no feeding frequency.
note.zh: 有报告记录弹涂鱼趁机会取食 Episesarma 蟹，但未给出取食频率。

note.en: Herons can catch and eat giant mudskippers.
Arrows show possible food paths. A missing path here does not mean an animal will die.
note.zh: 箭头表示可能的食物路径。图中路径中断，不表示动物一定会死亡。
